Done. Both the skill reference and memory are updated.

Summary of what I learned and saved:

Root cause: My USD extraction was correct (sum = 573,088 million USD for UK Total Liabilities June 2000+2001+2002). The error was purely the **FX rate**: I used 0.67 GBP/USD instead of the correct 0.65. The actual USD→GBP spot on June 30, 2002 was ~0.6547 (1 GBP ≈ 1.527 USD), which rounds to 0.65. The 0.67 value corresponds to an earlier date in 2001/early-2002 when GBP was weaker — I retrieved the rate from the wrong date. This caused a +3.2% overshoot (384510.06 vs 372507.20).

Generalizable lesson (saved to both the `capital-movements-liabilities-by-country-fx-convert.md` reference and memory): when a question pins an FX rate "as of June 30, 2002," retrieve the spot for that EXACT date, not a nearby month average or a value carried over from an earlier period. Even a 2-cent rounding-bucket difference (0.65 vs 0.67) tanks the answer. I pinned the exact constants: USD_sum=573088, rate=0.65.
